Advisory service

Insurance Portfolio Review for Businesses

A portfolio review compares the insurance you hold with the risks you actually carry. It is most useful 6 to 8 weeks before renewal, when there is still time to change course.

What we do

  • Read your policy schedules and key wording
  • Compare sums insured with realistic replacement values
  • Spot gaps, such as an activity with no liability cover
  • Spot overlaps that add cost without adding protection
  • Check contract and tender insurance requirements against what you hold
  • Prepare a renewal strategy and approach insurers for terms where you ask us to

How it works

  1. Share your documents

    Send what you have. We tell you what is missing.

  2. We review

    We map your risks to your covers and list gaps and questions.

  3. We explain

    You get a clear summary in plain language with recommendations.

  4. You decide

    We act only on what you instruct, including approaching insurers.

What to have ready

  • Current policy schedules (and wording where available)
  • Renewal dates and premiums paid
  • Asset, stock and payroll summaries
  • Claims record for recent years
  • Contracts that specify insurance

Please note

  • A review is advice on information you provide. It does not guarantee lower premiums or claim outcomes.
  • Insurers decide whether to offer terms and on what basis.

Questions

Do I need to change my broker or agent to get a review?

No. You can ask for a review of your existing programme. If changes are worthwhile, we explain them and you decide.

What does it cost?

Please ask us. Any fees or remuneration arrangements will be explained to you before you proceed.
